subject: EU anchoring: operational playbook + DPA addendum for transient egress
messages:
From: Claire D'Souza <claire@medassist.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <dpo@medassist.com>, MedAssist Legal <legal@medassist.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:04:00 +0100
Subject: Residency assurance and temporary egress window questions

Rafael —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope production onboarding we need clarity on a few residency items before Legal signs the DPA:

- Can Redwood guarantee that production traffic will be anchored to the EU (data-at-rest + processing) for our EU customers?
- Under what operational conditions would Redwood perform transient processing outside the EU (e.g., failover, autoscale, cache warmup)? We have a hard preference for no cross-border processing unless there is a documented, time-limited exception.
- We also need a current subprocessor roster and an indication of whether any subprocessors are outside the EU today.

Please attach any short operational playbook that describes the controls, timelines, and evidence we can expect. Priya (DPO) is copied for compliance questions.

Claire
Claire D'Souza
Head of Platform Integrations — MedAssist Health
claire@medassist.com

Attachment: MedAssist_Questions_Residency.docx (referenced)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@medassist.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <dpo@medassist.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and temporary egress window questions

Claire — thanks, and great questions. High-level summary below and I've attached a short operational playbook and our current subprocessor roster for your review.

Summary (short):
- Residency anchoring: primary storage and model inference for EU-tenant data is pinned to EU regions (Frankfurt/Paris).
- Transient egress: we support a controlled, documented transient egress window (72 hours maximum) for urgent failover / burst scenarios when EU capacity is exhausted. This is opt-in per-customer and scoped in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: roster attached; the majority of infra subprocessors for EU tenants operate in-region. A small set of telemetry/monitoring vendors process aggregated signals from outside the EU — we can provide SAs and SCCs.

What I'm attaching:
- Redwood_Residency_Playbook_v1.pdf — step-by-step operational controls, notification timelines, and evidence produced during a transient egress event.
- subprocessor_roster_Q3.xlsx — names, roles, country of processing, contact for evidence requests.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priya: can you confirm whether the 72-hour transient egress cap aligns with MedAssist's risk tolerance, or whether you need a shorter window?
2) Kimberly: loop Legal to review DPA addendum we can prepare.
3) Claire: confirm the countersigning contact and preferred Docusign cadence.

Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps; otherwise we'll prepare the DPA addendum for your review.

— Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_Residency_Playbook_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_Q3.xlsx

From: Priya Nair <dpo@medassist.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Claire D'Souza <claire@medassist.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 12:37:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and temporary egress window questions

Rafael / Claire —

Thanks, Rafael. A few clarifying items from a DPO perspective before Legal will approve the addendum:

1) Scope of data: we need the playbook to explicitly list which data classes are eligible for transient egress (e.g., anonymized telemetry vs. PII). Our expectation: no PII leaves the EU except under the most limited failover conditions and only for in-flight inference that cannot be completed otherwise.
2) Auditability: we need immutable audit logs for any transient egress event (timestamps, affected tenant IDs, token/sequence ranges where possible). Is there a mechanism to produce a per-event audit package?
3) Cryptography: customer-managed KEKs (KMS) preferred for the primary EU storage — can Redwood support customer KMS for EU tenants?
4) SOC2 / ISO evidence: please point us to the latest reports or the security pack.

If you can add the explicit answers in the playbook and provide the SOC2 evidence link, I can move this to Legal review.

Regards,
Priya Nair
Data Protection Officer — MedAssist Health
dpo@medassist.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and temporary egress window questions (internal)

Rafael / Kim —

Internal note on Priya's asks and recommended controls:

- Data classes: we should classify which tables/streams are allowed in an egress event. I propose a whitelist: only anonymized inference payloads and ephemeral KV cache replicas used for warmup. No customer PII should be eligible.
- Audit package: we can produce a per-event bundle (audit logs + packet list + region-handoff timestamps). Format: signed JSON + zipped logs. That meets legal evidence needs.
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in EU; must include key rotation and HSM-backed KEKs for production.
- SOC2: point customers to https://redwood.app/security/soc2 (we have the report and summary available through NDA).

Operational ask: Kimberly please draft a short clause for the DPA addendum stating: "Transient cross-border processing limited to specified non-PII caches for a maximum 72 hours, customer notification within 30 minutes, and delivery of audit package within 48 hours of event close."

I'll standby to provide the technical appendix to the playbook.

Ben Carter
Security — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@medassist.com>, Priya Nair <dpo@medassist.com>, MedAssist Legal <legal@medassist.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 15:20:00 +0100
Subject: Final operational commitments + DPA addendum (DocuSign)

Claire / Priya / MedAssist Legal —

Following internal review, please find the commitments and next steps below. I summarized Ben's technical inputs and attached the DPA addendum (Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf) for signature.

Committed points:
- Residency: production storage and inference for MedAssist EU tenants will be pinned to EU regions (Frankfurt / Paris) by default.
- Transient egress: a customer-opted transient egress policy (max 72 hours) limited to non-PII caches and anonymized inference payloads. No PII will be processed outside the EU except under an explicit emergency escalation with Exec-level approval.
- Auditability: Redwood will deliver an audit package for any transient egress event within 48 hours (signed logs + region timestamps + affected tenant IDs).
- KMS: customer-managed KMS in EU is supported (HSM-backed KEKs).
- Subprocessors: roster attached; any onboarding of new non-EU subprocessors that would affect MedAssist will require 30 days' notification and a right-to-review under the addendum.

Next steps (action owners):
- Redwood (Rafael / Kimberly): send DPA addendum via DocuSign (link below) and a final playbook PDF. Link: https://app.docusign.com/link/abc123-dpa-addendum
- MedAssist (Priya / Legal): review & sign addendum; indicate if 72-hour cap must be shortened.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare the technical appendix for audit packages and provide SOC2 access under NDA.

If that aligns, we'll kick the DocuSign flow today.
